newsitem.title: USA: U.S. late Brent trade boosts June outright prices.
newsitem.headline: U.S. late Brent trade boosts June outright prices.

text.p: Late North Sea Brent crude trade in the U.S. bolstered outright prices paid for June paper cargoes on Monday, according to foreign crude players.
A deal for a full cargo of June Brent was recorded at $18.30 a barrel, with a Wall Streeter the buyer from a U.K. major, traders said.
June exchange for physicals (EFP's) were also heard sold from $18.26-30 for a total of 900 lots in five separate transactions.
Other trades were confirmed for June/July inter-month Brent spreads, twice at minus 11 cents and once at minus 10 cents, traders said.
IPE June Brent settled 1 cent lower at $18.26 a barrel.
